description: obFMU is an occupant behaviour modelling tool packaged as a functional mock-up unit, so any building energy modelling program that implements the Functional Mock-up Interface (FMI) can call it during co-simulation. It reads behaviour models written in obXML, an XML schema built on the drivers-needs-actions-systems (DNAS) ontology, and contains the co-simulation interface, a data model and solvers. The paper by Hong and co-authors demonstrates it with occupants switching lights, opening and closing windows and switching air conditioners. Coverage: generic behaviours defined by the user. Access: downloads of obFMU and obXML, with documentation and examples, are listed on LBNL's behaviour research site, which could not be reached here. Licence: not read. Caveats: behaviour models must be specified and calibrated by the user, and the tool is research software. Simulation uses: adding stochastic occupant actions to energy simulations to narrow gaps between simulated and measured energy use. Related records: the LBNL Occupancy Simulator and EnergyPlus.
